controls.title: IT Governance
controls.description: Policies and controls governing IT security management, roles, responsibilities, and risk management across Singapore Government agencies.

controls.title: IT Security Policy
controls.description: The agency shall establish, document, and maintain an IT security policy that is approved by senior management, communicated to all staff, and reviewed at least annually or upon significant changes.

controls.title: IT Security Risk Management
controls.description: The agency shall conduct an IT security risk assessment at least annually or when there are significant system or environment changes. Residual risks must be formally accepted by the system owner.

controls.title: IT Security Roles and Responsibilities
controls.description: The agency shall designate an IT Security Manager (ITSM) and define security roles and responsibilities for all staff. Segregation of duties shall be enforced for critical functions.

controls.title: IT Security Awareness and Training
controls.description: All staff with access to government systems shall complete IT security awareness training annually. Staff in security-sensitive roles shall receive role-specific training.

controls.title: IT Security Audit
controls.description: The agency shall conduct periodic IT security audits and vulnerability assessments. Findings shall be tracked to remediation. Penetration testing shall be conducted at least annually for internet-facing systems.

controls.title: System Baseline and Configuration Standards
controls.description: All systems shall be configured according to an approved security baseline. Deviations from baseline must be documented and approved. Configuration reviews shall be conducted at least annually.

controls.title: Software Asset Management
controls.description: The agency shall maintain an inventory of all licensed software. Unlicensed or end-of-life software shall not be used in production environments.

controls.title: Access Control
controls.description: Controls governing user access provisioning, authentication, privileged access management, and remote access to government systems.

controls.title: User Access Management
controls.description: User accounts shall be provisioned based on least privilege and business need-to-know. Access rights shall be reviewed at least every six months and revoked promptly upon cessation of employment or role change.

controls.title: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
controls.description: MFA shall be enforced for all administrative access, remote access, and access to sensitive government systems and data. Single-factor authentication is not permitted for privileged accounts.

controls.title: Privileged Access Management
controls.description: Privileged accounts (admin, root, service accounts) shall be inventoried, managed through a Privileged Access Management (PAM) solution, and subject to enhanced monitoring. Shared privileged accounts are prohibited.

controls.title: Password and Credential Policy
controls.description: Password policy shall enforce minimum complexity (12+ characters, mixed case, numbers, symbols), maximum validity of 90 days for privileged accounts, and prohibition of password reuse for the last 12 passwords.

controls.title: Remote Access Security
controls.description: Remote access to government systems shall use government-approved VPN or secure gateway with MFA. All remote sessions shall be logged. Direct RDP/SSH exposure to the internet is prohibited.

controls.title: Identity and Access Governance
controls.description: The agency shall implement identity governance controls including access certification, role-based access control (RBAC), and just-in-time (JIT) provisioning for sensitive environments.

controls.title: Service Account Management
controls.description: Service accounts shall use unique credentials, follow least privilege, and not be used for interactive logon. Service account credentials shall be rotated at least annually and stored in an approved secrets management solution.

controls.title: Network Security
controls.description: Controls governing government intranet, internet connectivity, network segmentation, and secure communications.

controls.title: Network Segmentation and Zoning
controls.description: Government networks shall be segmented into security zones (Internet, DMZ, Intranet, Restricted). Traffic between zones shall be controlled by firewalls with deny-by-default rules. Network diagrams shall be maintained and reviewed annually.

controls.title: Firewall and Gateway Management
controls.description: Firewalls shall be configured with minimum necessary rules. Firewall rule reviews shall be conducted at least every six months. Internet-facing services shall be placed in a DMZ.

controls.title: Internet Access Controls
controls.description: Internet access from government networks shall go through an approved Secure Web Gateway (SWG) with content filtering, malware scanning, and SSL inspection. Proxy bypass is prohibited without approval.

controls.title: Email Security
controls.description: Government email systems shall implement SPF, DKIM, and DMARC. Anti-spam, anti-phishing, and anti-malware controls shall be applied. Sensitive data shall not be transmitted via unencrypted email.

controls.title: Wireless Network Security
controls.description: Wireless networks shall use WPA3 or WPA2-Enterprise with 802.1X authentication. Guest wireless networks shall be isolated from the government intranet. Rogue access point detection shall be implemented.

controls.title: DNS Security
controls.description: Government DNS infrastructure shall implement DNSSEC for authoritative zones. DNS filtering shall be used to block access to known malicious domains. Internal DNS resolvers shall not be exposed to the internet.

controls.title: System and Endpoint Security
controls.description: Controls governing endpoint protection, patch management, and system hardening for government devices and servers.

controls.title: Patch and Vulnerability Management
controls.description: Critical and high severity patches shall be applied within 30 days of release. Medium severity patches shall be applied within 90 days. An exception process with compensating controls is required for systems that cannot be patched within the timeline.

controls.title: Endpoint Protection
controls.description: All government endpoints (workstations, laptops, servers) shall have approved antivirus/EDR solutions installed with real-time protection enabled and definitions updated daily. USB and removable media controls shall be implemented.

controls.title: System Hardening
controls.description: All systems shall be hardened according to approved CIS Benchmarks or equivalent. Unnecessary services, ports, and accounts shall be disabled. Operating system hardening guides shall be applied before system deployment.

controls.title: Mobile Device Management
controls.description: Government mobile devices shall be enrolled in an approved Mobile Device Management (MDM) solution. Remote wipe capability shall be enabled. Personal devices used for government work (BYOD) shall comply with MDM policy.

controls.title: Vulnerability Scanning
controls.description: Authenticated vulnerability scans shall be conducted monthly on all internet-facing and sensitive internal systems. Scan results shall be reviewed and critical/high findings remediated within defined SLAs.

controls.title: Application Security
controls.description: Controls governing secure software development, application security testing, and API security for government digital services.

controls.title: Secure Software Development Lifecycle (SSDLC)
controls.description: The agency shall implement a Secure Software Development Lifecycle (SSDLC) incorporating security requirements, threat modelling, secure design review, and security testing at each phase before deployment.

controls.title: Application Security Testing
controls.description: Static Application Security Testing (SAST) shall be performed during development. Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST) and penetration testing shall be conducted before go-live and at least annually for production systems.

controls.title: Open Source and Third-Party Component Security
controls.description: Software Composition Analysis (SCA) shall be performed to identify and remediate known vulnerabilities in open source and third-party libraries. Dependency versions shall be tracked and kept updated.

controls.title: API Security
controls.description: APIs shall implement authentication (OAuth 2.0 / API keys), rate limiting, input validation, and output encoding. API inventory shall be maintained. Sensitive data shall not be exposed in API responses beyond what is necessary.

controls.title: Web Application Security
controls.description: Public-facing web applications shall be protected by a Web Application Firewall (WAF). OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities shall be addressed. Security headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options) shall be configured.

controls.title: Secrets and Credential Management
controls.description: Application secrets, API keys, and database credentials shall be stored in an approved secrets management solution (e.g., Azure Key Vault). Hardcoded credentials in source code are prohibited and enforced via SAST/secrets scanning.

controls.title: Secure Code Repository Management
controls.description: Source code repositories shall enforce branch protection, require pull request reviews, and integrate with SAST and secrets scanning pipelines. Public exposure of government source code repositories is prohibited without approval.

controls.title: Data and Information Security
controls.description: Controls governing government data classification, handling, encryption, and data loss prevention.

controls.title: Data Classification
controls.description: All government data shall be classified according to the Government Data Classification Framework (GDCF): Restricted, Confidential, Official, or Public. Data handling requirements shall be applied based on classification.

controls.title: Data Encryption at Rest
controls.description: Data classified as Confidential or Restricted shall be encrypted at rest using AES-256 or equivalent. Database encryption and full-disk encryption shall be implemented on all systems storing sensitive government data.

controls.title: Data Encryption in Transit
controls.description: All data transmissions involving government data shall use TLS 1.2 or higher. TLS 1.0 and 1.1 are prohibited. Certificate management shall include automated renewal and monitoring for expiry.

controls.title: Data Loss Prevention (DLP)
controls.description: DLP controls shall be implemented to prevent unauthorised exfiltration of sensitive government data via email, web upload, removable media, and cloud storage. DLP policies shall be tuned to data classification labels.

controls.title: Data Retention and Disposal
controls.description: Government data shall be retained according to the Government Records Management Framework. Data disposal shall use approved methods (DoD 5220.22-M or equivalent for electronic media; physical destruction for classified media).

controls.title: Personal Data Protection
controls.description: Systems processing personal data shall comply with the Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA) and government personal data protection policies. Data minimisation, purpose limitation, and subject access controls shall be implemented.

controls.title: Database Security
controls.description: Databases storing government data shall implement access controls, audit logging, and activity monitoring. Database queries shall use parameterised statements. Database access from application accounts shall follow least privilege.

controls.title: Government Commercial Cloud (GCC) Security
controls.description: Controls specific to Singapore Government Commercial Cloud (GCC) environments including AWS GCC, Azure GCC, and GCC+.

controls.title: Cloud Service Approval and Onboarding
controls.description: Cloud services used by government agencies shall be approved by GovTech and onboarded through the Government Commercial Cloud (GCC) programme. Unapproved cloud services (Shadow IT) are prohibited for government data.

controls.title: Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM)
controls.description: Cloud environments shall be monitored continuously using approved CSPM tools. Cloud misconfiguration findings shall be remediated within defined SLAs. Cloud security benchmarks (CIS AWS/Azure/GCP) shall be applied.

controls.title: Cloud Identity and Access Management
controls.description: Cloud IAM shall follow least privilege. Root/global administrator accounts shall use MFA and not be used for routine operations. Service accounts and managed identities shall be used in place of long-lived access keys.

controls.title: Cloud Data Residency and Sovereignty
controls.description: Government data classified Restricted or above shall remain within approved GCC regions (Singapore). Data replication to non-approved regions is prohibited without explicit GovTech approval.

controls.title: Cloud Network Security Controls
controls.description: Cloud virtual networks shall implement security groups/NSGs with deny-by-default. Public-facing resources shall be protected by WAF and DDoS protection. Network flow logs shall be enabled for all VPCs/VNets.

controls.title: Serverless and Container Security
controls.description: Serverless functions and containers shall be scanned for vulnerabilities using approved tools. Container images shall be pulled from approved registries. Runtime security monitoring shall be implemented for containerised workloads.

controls.title: Cloud Key Management
controls.description: Cryptographic keys used in cloud environments shall be managed through cloud-native KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault). Customer-managed keys (CMK) shall be used for government-classified data. Key rotation shall be automated.

controls.title: Security Logging and Monitoring
controls.description: Controls governing security event logging, SIEM integration, and continuous monitoring of government systems.

controls.title: Security Event Logging
controls.description: All government systems shall enable security event logging covering authentication events, privilege escalation, system changes, and data access. Logs shall be retained for at least 12 months (online) and 5 years (archived).

controls.title: Centralised Log Management (SIEM)
controls.description: Security logs from all in-scope systems shall be forwarded to a centralised SIEM. SIEM use cases shall cover critical attack patterns including brute force, lateral movement, and data exfiltration. Alerts shall be triaged within defined SLAs.

controls.title: Log Integrity and Tamper Protection
controls.description: Security logs shall be stored in an immutable, tamper-evident manner. Write access to log stores shall be restricted. Log forwarding shall be monitored for gaps or failures.

controls.title: Security Operations and Threat Monitoring
controls.description: The agency shall establish or subscribe to a Security Operations Centre (SOC) function with 24/7 monitoring capability for critical systems. Threat intelligence feeds shall be integrated into monitoring.

controls.title: Privileged Activity Monitoring
controls.description: All privileged user activity (admin logins, configuration changes, access to sensitive data) shall be logged and reviewed. Privileged session recording shall be implemented for critical systems.

controls.title: Incident Management
controls.description: Controls governing cybersecurity incident detection, response, reporting, and recovery for government agencies.

controls.title: Incident Response Plan
controls.description: The agency shall maintain a documented Cybersecurity Incident Response Plan (CIRP) that is reviewed and tested at least annually. The plan shall define incident classification, escalation procedures, and roles.

controls.title: Incident Reporting to GovTech
controls.description: Cybersecurity incidents affecting government systems shall be reported to GovTech / SingCERT within defined timeframes: Critical incidents within 1 hour, High within 4 hours, Medium within 24 hours.

controls.title: Incident Containment and Eradication
controls.description: Incident response procedures shall include containment, eradication, and recovery steps. Forensic evidence shall be preserved. Root cause analysis shall be completed and lessons learned documented within 30 days.

controls.title: Tabletop Exercises and Drills
controls.description: The agency shall conduct cybersecurity incident simulation exercises (tabletop or functional) at least annually to validate the Incident Response Plan and team readiness.

controls.title: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery
controls.description: Controls governing IT business continuity planning, backup management, and disaster recovery for government digital services.

controls.title: Business Continuity Plan (BCP)
controls.description: The agency shall maintain a Business Continuity Plan covering critical IT systems. The BCP shall define Recovery Time Objectives (RTO) and Recovery Point Objectives (RPO) and be reviewed annually.

controls.title: Backup and Recovery
controls.description: Critical government data and systems shall be backed up regularly (daily minimum for critical systems). Backups shall be encrypted and stored in a separate location. Recovery restoration shall be tested at least annually.

controls.title: Disaster Recovery Testing
controls.description: Disaster recovery exercises shall be conducted at least annually for critical government systems. DR test results shall be documented and used to improve DR plans. RTO and RPO targets shall be validated during tests.

controls.title: Third Party and Supply Chain Security
controls.description: Controls governing vendor risk management, cloud service provider requirements, and IT outsourcing security for government agencies.

controls.title: Vendor Security Assessment
controls.description: Third-party vendors with access to government systems or data shall undergo a security assessment before onboarding and at least every two years. Security requirements shall be included in contracts.

controls.title: Third-Party Access Controls
controls.description: Third-party access to government systems shall be provisioned on a just-in-time basis with MFA enforced. All third-party sessions shall be logged and monitored. Access shall be revoked immediately upon contract end.

controls.title: Software Supply Chain Security
controls.description: The agency shall assess the security of software supply chains including open source libraries and commercial software. Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) shall be requested for critical software products.

controls.title: Outsourced IT Operations Security
controls.description: IT outsourcing agreements shall include security requirements, right-to-audit clauses, breach notification obligations, and compliance with IM8. Outsourced operations shall be subject to periodic security reviews.
